newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end near lows on thin volume.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end near lows on thin volume.

text.p: *Shares closed weaker, the market unable to recover from a Wall Street-inspired fall. Total volume 245.5 million shares worth A$446.3 million, 937 stocks traded, 318 steady, 255 rises, 364 falls
Australian shares ended near their lows for the day after buying dried up in the afternoon session, dashing promising signs of recovery around midday.
The key market barometer, the All Ordinaries index closed 12 points down at 2,256.7, near its intra-day low of 2,254.8.
The September share price index finished seven points down at 2,254, a 2.7 point discount to the underlying index.

Brokers said the light volume reflected the lack of interest in the market ahead of the U.S. Labor Day holiday on Monday and speculation about the possibility of a local interest rate cut later this week.
"Australian investors face a confusing time with the prospect of rising rates in the U.S., but lower rates at home," a Melbourne-based dealer said.
The dealer said in the medium term he expected the market to continue to rise as investors built in the positive effects of the federal government's budget policy of fiscal restraint.

"In my opinion, shares are still coming from a low base and even though there could be some short term uncertainty the market still has a long way to go before it no longer is undervalued," the dealer said.
The industrial sector, although ending weaker, outperformed the resource sector on the day and was supported by the resilience of media and insurance stocks.
In particular, media group News Corp continued to do well on the back of the success of its alien invasion movie 'Independence Day'.

Local currency and bonds were influenced mainly by speculation a Reserve bank board meeting on Tuesday could clear the way for rates to be cut again. The Australian dollar slipped below the key US$0.79 level while bonds largely fended off the effects of a U.S. bond market slide.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivative trade was subdued ahead of the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
Turnover in September SPI futures totalled 4,812 (7,883).

Major banks ended lower as investors took profits due to competitive outlook for bank sector.
Paper firm's shares ended down on lower year profit release.
Miners ended down but off lows on talk of local rate cut.
Insurance group's shares surged after the company reported strong year earnings and one-for-four bonus issue.
Betting agency's shares rose after strong year profit release.
Drug firm's shares climbed on expectation the company will move to phase III trials of its influenza drug, GG167.
Air New Zealand Ltd AIRa.NZ confirmed it would buy TNT's 50 percent stake in Ansett for a total A$475 million, subject to Australian regulatory approval.
